page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, with 32 physical cores and hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 2048.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 32.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage consists of a 1900 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the instance supports a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data shows strong multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 61947.26 and a PassMark CPU score of 56826.42. Single-core performance is average, as reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 1688.0. The instance demonstrates strong capabilities in specialized tasks, achieving high scores in software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations. Memory bandwidth benchmarks are average, with read-only large block speeds at 153.34 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 61.06 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers high memory allocation relative to compute resources, making it a specialized option for memory-bound workloads. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage and high baseline network bandwidth provides integrated high-speed storage without relying solely on network-attached volumes. However, the trade-off lies in the average single-core performance and average memory bandwidth scores, indicating that workloads requiring extreme single-threaded speed may not fully utilize the massive memory footprint.

This configuration is suitable for memory-intensive applications, including large-scale in-memory databases, big data analytics, enterprise-grade relational databases, and memory-bound electronic design automation workloads. The high multi-core performance and local NVMe storage also support intensive database operations and software compilation pipelines.
